findings.message:
Task acceptance not fulfilled: the review found that the candidate does not satisfy source issue #1211. Change the candidate so it satisfies everything the issue requires; the reviewer's acceptance evidence:
- `ops/gpg-dsh.sh` has the same blob `b073fedd8e085f6f0d133e0d65c55199fd5cb04a` at base `db01eb0` and head `7e793fa`, so no validation guard was added.
- The only changed path is `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts`, which adds regression cases asserting no `gpgconf` invocation.
- `ops/gpg-dsh.sh` line 178 still calls `gpgconf --homedir $legacy_seed --kill gpg-agent` after `has_legacy_seed`, so a symlinked or missing legacy seed with an owned sibling leftover still follows the link to the real GnuPG homedir.
- The new assertions at `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts` line 833 expect `[]` from `gpgconfCalls`, which the unchanged helper cannot satisfy.

[P1] Added legacy cleanup tests assert a guard that does not exist

The eight new cases assert `gpgconfCalls(fixture)` is empty, but `ops/gpg-dsh.sh` is byte-identical to base (blob `b073fedd8e085f6f0d133e0d65c55199fd5cb04a`): `discard_legacy_seed` still runs `gpgconf --homedir $legacy_seed --kill gpg-agent` unconditionally whenever `has_legacy_seed` succeeds, and that function succeeds when the legacy seed is a symlink or missing while a sibling `.lock`/`.lock.break`/`.new.*`/`.old.*` directory is owned. Every added case therefore fails when run, so this change reddens the suite without fixing the symlink-following agent shutdown the tests describe.

tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts:825-833

summary: The change adds only regression tests for issue 1211; the required owned_dir guard in ops/gpg-dsh.sh is absent, so the new tests fail and the reported symlink-following agent shutdown is unfixed.

The new assertions at `tests/gpg-dsh.test.ts` line 833 expect `[]` from `gpgconfCalls`, which the unchanged helper cannot satisfy.
